title: Thieves steal Renaissance masterpieces from Messina museum
summary: Four paintings attributed to Renaissance master Antonello da Messina remain missing after a daring theft from the Museo Regionale di Messina in Sicily, where investigators are now examining surveillance footage and the circumstances surrounding the security breach. The crime has struck at the heart of a collection closely connected to Messina’s own turbulent history. The museum preserves hundreds of works tracing the city’s cultural development, including objects rescued from the destruction caused by the catastrophic 1908 earthquake. Among its best-known holdings are paintings by Antonello, who was born in Messina, as well as major works by Caravaggio. At the center of the investigation is Antonello’s Polittico di San Gregorio, or San Gregorio Polyptych, a signed and dated work from 1473. title: New Berlin exhibition explores five centuries of portraiture and identity
summary: How do we see ourselves – and how have people in different historical periods wished to be seen? The special exhibition “Portraits! Surprising Encounters from Botticelli to Lempicka at the Gemäldegalerie (Old Master Paintings) ‒ Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, invites viewers on a fascinating journey through the history of portraiture. Unusual juxtapositions of works spanning five centuries reveal striking similarities, bringing the pieces to life and providing opportunities to reflect on the presentation of the self and others, as well as on staging, roles, and character. Masterpieces by artists such as Botticelli and Lempicka, Mino da Fiesole and Rogier van der Weyden, Dürer and Giorgione, or Rubens and Gainsborough are brought into conversation with one another, revealing striking and often surprising affinities. title: MoMA to honor director Steven Spielberg at 2026 Film Benefit
summary: The Museum of Modern Art’s 2026 Film Benefit, presented by CHANEL, will honor Academy Award–winning director and producer Steven Spielberg on November 12. Spielberg is one of the most successful and influential filmmakers in history, having directed more than 35 feature films and earned three Academy Awards and a record nine nominations for Best Director, including wins for Schindler’s List (1993) and Saving Private Ryan (1998). As a producer, he holds the record for the most Best Picture nominations at 14 total, including a win for Schindler’s List. For over 50 years his films—including Lincoln (2012), Bridge of Spies (2015), The Post (2017), West Side Story (2021), and The Fabelmans (2022)—have generated multiple Academy Award nominations. Most recently, he directed this summer's original science fiction hit, Disclosure Day (2026). Spielberg is one of few to achieve EGOT status, having won at least one Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony

title: Maria Lassnig and Edvard Munch in dialogue for the first time
summary: From 2 October 2026 to 21 February 2027, the Kunsthaus Zürich presents the first exhibition to directly relate the works of the Austrian painter Maria Lassnig and the Norwegian artist Edvard Munch. Some 150 exhibits open up a fascinating dialogue around the body, perception and the cycle of life – and establish a new relationship between two exceptional artistic stances. At the same time, the presentation is a reminder that the Kunsthaus is the custodian of a remarkable treasure: the largest collection of Munch paintings outside Norway. ‘Maria Lassnig and Edvard Munch. Flow of Paint = Flow of Life’ at the Kunsthaus Zürich is the first-ever double presentation showcasing the work of Austrian artist Maria Lassnig (1919–2014) alongside that of Norwegian painter Edvard Munch (1863–1944). title: Explore Eric Carle's Modern art inspirations & creative influences in a new exhibition
summary: A new exhibition at The Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art examines the movements and artists that shaped Eric Carle’s distinctive visual language. On view September 19, 2026 – September 5, 2027, Eric Carle’s Modernist Inspirations traces his formative years in Germany, when his high school art teacher secretly introduced him to the work of so-called “degenerate” artists banned by the regime, making a lasting impression on Carle’s own work. The exhibition highlights his admiration for the Bauhaus school and Der Blaue Reiter (The Blue Rider) group, presenting selections from his oeuvre in dialogue with works by modernist figures such as Anni Albers, Marc Chagall, Sonia Delaunay, Fujimori Shizuo, Paul Klee, Oscar Kokoschka, Fernand Léger, August Macke, René Magritte, Franz Marc, and Pablo Picasso, all on loan from area museums. title: Can art help us understand death?
summary: "Death is a broad-ranging topic. Historically, art has dealt with death in many ways, such as memento mori and the Dance of Death, but here we would rather show how our relationship with death is constantly influenced by technology, religion and cultural expression," says Geir Haraldseth, curator at the National Museum. “Don’t be afraid. An exhibition about death” consists of nearly a hundred works, from antiquity via national romanticism to contemporary art. Here, the audience encounters works from the National Museum’s collection in a new setting. "We want to show that there is leeway in how we think, speak and relate to death. There is something beautiful in the fact that all cultures have always had rituals around this, and that they change along with society. In encountering this exhibition, we hope that the audience uses both their heart and their head," says Ingrid Røynesdal, director of the National Museum. "Don't be afraid. title: The Cleveland Museum of Art begins comprehensive restoration of historical fine arts garden
summary: The Cleveland Museum of Art today announced the beginning of the first phase of a multiyear restoration of its historical Fine Arts Garden, one of Cleveland’s most celebrated public landscapes. On August 24, the museum begins implementation of an important phase of the CMA Landscape Master Plan, an ambitious initiative to preserve, restore, and renew the museum’s iconic Fine Arts Garden, enhancing accessibility, ecological sustainability, and the visitor experience. The work marks the first major investment in the museum’s historical landscape in nearly a century and represents an important milestone in the CMA’s long-term commitment to preserving one of Northeast Ohio’s most treasured outdoor civic spaces. title: Perrotin New York to present solo exhibition Menagerie by Nikki Maloof
summary: Perrotin New York will present Menagerie, an exhibition by Nikki Maloof. The artist’s new body of paintings presents a world where imagined interiors and fantastical landscapes become proxies for the human experience and our repressed animal instincts. Over the last few years Maloof has expanded her intimate painterly universe to include vast country landscapes. In this new body of work, she moves into public spaces, including a zoo and a restaurant. Every day, Maloof drops her daughters off at school before heading to her backyard studio in Massachusetts. There she follows the crumbs of her own desires. She plays around with paint until a metallic pattern emerges, reminding her of a grid. title: Walker Art Center presents Olalekan Jeyifous: Hydrocosmic Litanies
summary: The Walker Art Center opened artist, architect, and designer Olalekan Jeyifous’s (US, b. Nigeria, 1977) first museum solo exhibition, entitled Hydrocosmic Litanies. Jeyifous, who won the prestigious Silver Lion at the 2023 Venice Architecture Biennale, is recognized for reimagining social spaces with consideration toward the dynamic relationships between architecture, community, and the environment. Through his wide-ranging, multidisciplinary work, Jeyifous explores how engagement with and construction of natural and human-made spaces can address critical issues of social equity and ecological justice. title: C/O Berlin to present double exhibition by After Nature prize winners
summary: C/O Berlin will present the double exhibition of the winners of the After Nature . Ulrike Crespo Photography Prize 26: Stelios Kallinikou. Cliffs Among Dreams and Susanne Kriemann . Im Fieber der Sonne flattern Schmetterlinge im Bauch from Sep 12, 2026 to Jan 20, 2027. The opening takes place on Friday, Sep 11, 2026 at 20:00 at C/O Berlin in Amerika Haus. By recognizing the work of Stelios Kallinikou and Susanne Kriemann, C/O Berlin Foundation and Crespo Foundation are showcasing two artistic practices that intertwine temporalities. Both projects take us to places where the past persists into the present day: to regions under military control, contaminated landscapes, and into the very soil. These artists make palpable those conditions that cannot be apprehended with the senses, exploring how the photographic image might operate when what needs to be shown is invisible to the eye. title: Gropius Bau to host major Christoph Schlingensief exhibition in Berlin
summary: Through striking political actions and projects spanning theatre, opera, film and the visual arts, Christoph Schlingensief (1960–2010) turned an unflinching gaze upon the absurdities of the present. From 9 October 2026, Gropius Bau will present Es ist nicht mehr mein Problem, macht eure Scheiße alleine (It’s not my problem anymore, deal with your own shit), an exhibition illuminating his visionary, genre-defying body of work. The artist’s most comprehensive German showcase in over a decade, it is conceived not as a traditional retrospective, but as a dynamic dialogue between key groups of Schlingensief’s works. With this exhibition, Gropius Bau deepens its exploration of artistic approaches that operate across genres and deliberately transcend their boundaries. title: Gerald Peters Contemporary opens Indigenous group exhibition As We Have Always Been
summary: Gerald Peters Contemporary is presenting As We Have Always Been, bringing together four Indigenous voices whose practices offer distinct perspectives on identity, place, memory, and cultural continuity. Through varied artistic approaches, the exhibition considers the enduring relationships between ancestral knowledge, lived experience, and contemporary expression. Grounded in Indigenous perspectives, the exhibition explores how each artist draws upon personal histories, cultural traditions, and enduring relationships to land to examine questions of belonging, resilience, and self-definition. While distinct in their approaches, the works collectively reflect the vitality of contemporary Indigenous artistic practice, offering nuanced perspectives on continuity, stewardship, and the evolving nature of Indigenous identity across generations. title: USF Contemporary Art Museum to open Ellen Harvey retrospective
summary: PICTURE(SQUE): Ellen Harvey Works, 1999-2025 opens Monday, August 24 at USF Contemporary Art Museum, College of Design, Art & Performance, with an Artist Conversation and Exhibition Reception presented on Friday, August 28. The exhibition is on view through March 6, 2027. Admission is Free. A major exhibition of works by internationally acclaimed artist, Ellen Harvey, will open at USFCAM. Entitled PICTURE(SQUE), the exhibition spans more than two decades of work that spotlights the artist’s lifelong quest to draw attention to the revolutionary potential of nostalgia, the relationship between art and tourism, the role of art and the artist in our society, and the social and ecological implications of the picturesque. title: British Fashion Council launches Fashion Britain in Liverpool this September
summary: Following the announcement of Fashion Britain, the British Fashion Council (BFC) unveils a nationwide programme of events that will bring the initiative to life in Liverpool and six other cities this September. Developed as part of the BFC's Strategy 2030: Access, Creativity and Growth, Fashion Britain will celebrate the breadth of British creativity through a series of public designer conversations, cultural activations, retail experiences, exhibitions and live performances, celebrating the wealth of talent that has emerged across the UK. Laura Weir, Chief Executive, British Fashion Council: "I am incredibly excited for the launch of Fashion Britain this September. title: New Hales exhibition explores work of Boffin, Fani-Kayode, and Gupta
summary: Hales will present Staging Resistance, a look at Tessa Boffin's, Rotimi Fani-Kayode's and Sunil Gupta's trailblazing work from the 1980s, a pivotal moment for Queer British photography. The show coincides with Sunil Gupta's retrospective, Life with a Camera, 1970 - Now, on view at Kettle's Yard (Cambridge, UK) from September 2026 to January 2027, and Where We Touch the Archive, an ambitious touring project focused on the work of Tessa Boffin by Devonshire Collective, on view in Eastbourne, UK (July - September 2026). At the same time, Rotimi Fani-Kayode is featured in the Barbican Art Gallery's Project a Black Planet: The Art and Culture of Panafrica, (through September 2026, also touring to Art Institute of Chicago, MACBA Museu d'Art Contemporani de Barcelona and KANAL-Centre Pompidou Bruxelles). title: Galerie Nathalie Obadia to present solo exhibition Ferdinandea by Clément Cogitore
summary: Galerie Nathalie Obadia will present Ferdinandea in Paris, Clément Cogitore's first solo exhibition with the gallery. Following presentations at Madre - Museo d'Arte Contemporanea Donnaregina in Naples - and subsequently at Mucem in Marseille, under the title Clément Cogitore. Ferdinandea, l'île éphémère - on view until the end of September - this body of work continues its journey in Paris in a new configuration. A film, videos, archival documents and engraved photographs compose the narratives of an island whose imprint endures beyond its disappearance. Born in 1983 in Colmar (France), Clément Cogitore has developed a body of work at the crossroads of contemporary art and cinema. title: Tawan Wattuya explores value and currency in watercolor Money series at Nosbaum Reding
summary: Through watercolor and oil paint, Tawan Wattuya creates an aesthetics that arouses, excites while colliding with the senses, terrifying viewers, but also tickling them with caustic humor. A graduate of the Faculty of Painting, Sculpture, and Graphic Arts at Silpakorn University, Wattuya has exhibited widely both in Thailand and internationally. Wattuya's portraits and paintings are inspired by real people in the pop culture, whether it be beauty queens, stars and celebrities, politicians, or superheroes from cartoons and films, and of common people from all walks of life he met along his way, as well as records of events, both national and international alike. title: Templon to present Permanent Display, Robin Kid's fourth solo show with gallery
summary: Templon will present “Permanent Display”, Robin Kid’s fourth solo exhibition with the gallery. Conceived around the first presentation of works from his new LIFE series, the exhibition places a focused selection of works from the past decade into dialogue with this new body of work, allowing them to be encountered within a new constellation of meanings. Together, these works reveal the continuity of an artistic practice that examines how inherited cultural images shape our experience of the present. At the centre of the exhibition is LIFE, a new body of work developed by the artist over several years. Its conceptual origin can be traced to a lyric from The Doors’ 1968 song The Unknown Soldier: “Breakfast where the news is read, television children fed, bullet strikes the helmet’s head.” Compressing domestic routine, mass media, advertising, and political violence

title: Retrospective at Boise Art Museum highlights five decades of work by James Lavadour
summary: James Lavadour: Land of Origin is a career retrospective that surveys five decades of artwork by self-trained painter and printmaker James Lavadour (American, Walla Walla, b. 1951, Cayuse, OR). The paintings, prints, and multi-panel grids chart his creative output from the 1980s, when he became a full-time working artist, to his most recent artworks, created in 2025. His artistic practice is grounded in sustained looking, informed by walking, driving, stopping, and observing the landscape over the course of many decades, specifically the land of the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation, outside Pendleton, Oregon. Lavadour typically works on as many as fifty panels simultaneously, composing selections into harmonious multi-panel grids. title: Chinese Artists on the Edge film program highlights restored 1990s cinema
summary: Chinese Artists on the Edge brings together five landmark films that reveal the fertile exchange between contemporary art and Chinese cinema from the late 1980s through the turn of the twenty-first century. Most of these works were long unavailable or rarely screened, only recently returning to public view through restoration and archival preservation efforts. The program includes two films by Sixth Generation figurehead Zhang Yuan: his Beijing Film Academy student short White Lines (1988, 白线), a playful experiment starring neorealist painter Liu Xiaodong, and his seminal Beijing Bastards (1993, 北京杂种), an electrifying portrait of the capital's burgeoning rock music scene, revived through a recent digitization of the original 35mm print. title: SFMOMA acquires more than 90 works of Modern and Contemporary art
summary: The San Francisco Museum of Modern Art announced the acquisition of more than 90 modern and contemporary artworks, highlighting an incredible range of formal and conceptual innovations. The group continues SFMOMA’s commitment to platforming and enriching its holdings with global and local voices, adding both depth and new breadth to the museum’s growing collection. SFMOMA’s acquisitions over the past six months—from January to June 2026—include video installations and works by Stephanie Comilang and Simon Speiser, Alexandra Daisy Ginsberg, Ana Mendieta and Agnieszka Polska; works on paper by Arakawa + Gins and Orlando Smith; sculpture and mixed media works by Dan Friedman, Betye Saar, Nobuo Sekine, Kishio Suga, Finnegan Shannon, Rose B. title: Garrison Art Center presents group exhibition Phytophilia: The Love of Plants
summary: Garrison Art Center presents Phytophilia: The Love of Plants, a group exhibition by artists Lawre Stone, Janis Stemmermann, and Katharine Dufault. This exhibition brings together three artists working with the vegetal world as subject, refuge, and inspiration, exploring distinct ways of thinking and relating to both human and non-human beings. Employing landscape imagery, plant life, trees, and a feeling for spiritual phenomena, the artists of Phytophilia present a vision of a sentient, animate vegetal world, flourishing, communicating, nourishing and thriving in a post-human existence. Ultimately, their work reveals the deep vulnerability brought to the surface through human interactions with nature. title: Serralves presents its summer 2026 programme
summary: Serralves Museum of Contemporary Art presents a major summer programme bringing together three exhibitions that address some of the most urgent questions shaping contemporary experience: the political force of language, the instability of historical memory, and the representation of human identity in all its complexity. Together, Jenny Holzer: Wrong Answers, Vexation of Spirit—The Duerckheim Collection x Serralves, and Alice Neel: Beautifully Imperfect form a powerful constellation of exhibitions in which art becomes a means of confronting the present: its conflicts, omissions, distortions, and possibilities of resistance. Opening this summer, Jenny Holzer: Wrong Answers marks the celebrated American artist’s first solo exhibition in Portugal. title: Casco Art Institute announces Autumn 2026 exhibition The Land School
summary: Casco Art Institute: Working for the Commons presents its Autumn 2026 artistic program, The Land School, an exhibition and evolving collaboration between two collectives, the Amsterdam-based 4Siblings and Mexico City-based itacateca. Their shared engagement with land as pedagogy towards ecological regeneration and collective making forms the project's conceptual core. 4Siblings develops site-specific, land-based practices at the intersection of ecological thinking, pedagogy, and experimental forms of public art. Their work emerges through direct engagement with soil, plants, and local contexts as active collaborators, responding to questions of environmental decline, access to land, and the shifting conditions of contemporary artistic production.
